summary: This document modifies pseudowire VCCV signaling and selection so that proactive Connectivity Verification, Continuity Check, and Remote Defect Indication can be used over MPLS-TP while staying backward compatible.

eli5.summary: Network lines need regular wellness checks. This changes how devices agree on which checks to run without confusing older ones.

questions: which mpls-tp cv type has highest priority
subtitle: How two pseudowire edge routers agree to use MPLS-TP connectivity checks, without confusing older equipment.

tldr.problem: Proactive connectivity verification, continuity check and remote defect indication exist for the MPLS Transport Profile, but pseudowire VCCV signaling had no way to advertise or select them.
tldr.mechanism: A new VCCV Extended CV parameter (sub-TLV type 0x19) carries a bitmask of four new MPLS-TP CV types, and a priority list decides which one wins when both edge routers support several.
tldr.outcome: Pseudowires can use MPLS-TP CC-CV while staying backward compatible, and the MPLS-TP types take precedence over BFD CV types when both ends support both.

today: RFC 7189 is a Proposed Standard published in March 2014. No later RFC obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why VCCV Needs an Update
sections.content:
Proactive Connectivity Verification (CV), Continuity Check (CC) and Remote Defect Indication (RDI) for the MPLS Transport Profile are defined in RFC 6428. They apply to every construct of MPLS-TP, including pseudowires (PWs).

When a control plane sets up and manages PWs, the procedures of RFC 5085 and RFC 5885 pick the type of control channel and the matching type of connectivity verification. This document changes the signaling and selection steps so that proactive CV-CC-RDI can be used over MPLS-TP PWs and older implementations keep working.
sections.eli5: Some network lines already have a way to check they are alive. This RFC teaches the two ends a new, better way to check, and makes sure old equipment is not confused.

sections.title: The VCCV Extended CV Sub-TLV
sections.content:
PW VCCV can support several CV types, advertised in the CV Types field of the VCCV Interface Parameter sub-TLV. Six types had been defined. This document adds four more and defines a new VCCV Extended CV parameter for the PW Interface Parameters Sub-TLV to carry them.

The sub-TLV has a Type of 0x19, a Length, a CV Type bitmask and a Reserved field. Length covers the whole sub-TLV, including the type and length fields, and the minimum is 4. Extensions should be made in 4-byte increments. Reserved MUST be set to zeroes on transmit and ignored on receive.

The CV Type bitmask lists the kinds of CV monitoring a provider edge router (PE) can support. The sub-TLV MUST appear together with the VCCV parameter sub-TLV. If the VCCV parameter sub-TLV is missing, the extended sub-TLV SHOULD be ignored.
sections.eli5: It is a small form with tick boxes. Each tick box says one kind of check the router can do, and a blank part is left for the future.

sections.title: The Four MPLS-TP CC-CV Types
sections.content:
RFC 6428 defines coordinated and independent modes for monitoring a point-to-point bidirectional connection, and RFC 6310 defines how BFD-based OAM maps to the status of an Attachment Circuit. Combining the two modes with two kinds of functionality gives four CV types.

  • 0x01: independent mode, fault detection only.
  • 0x02: independent mode, fault detection and status signaling.
  • 0x04: coordinated mode, fault detection only.
  • 0x08: coordinated mode, fault detection and status signaling.
sections.eli5: There are two styles of checking and two jobs a check can do. Two styles times two jobs makes four kinds of check, each with its own tick box.

sections.title: Operation and CV Type Selection
sections.content:
MPLS-TP connectivity verification can be used with VCCV Control Channel Type 1. If that channel type is selected, PEs MAY select one of the MPLS-TP CC-CV types as the CV mechanism for the PW.

The selection rules of Section 7 of RFC 5085, updated by Section 4 of RFC 5885, are extended. If the common set of proactive CV types advertised by both PEs includes MPLS-TP CC-CV types and some BFD CV types, MPLS-TP CC-CV takes precedence over any BFD CV type. If several MPLS-TP types are common to both PEs, the highest priority is chosen from this list: 0x08, then 0x04, then 0x02, then 0x01.
sections.eli5: If both sides know several kinds of check, they use the fanciest one they share. The new kinds beat the older kinds.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content:
IANA reserved a new PW Interface Parameters Sub-TLV type, 0x19, with variable length, named VCCV Extended CV Parameter.

IANA also set up a registry of VCCV Extended CV Types. The values are 8 bits. Values 0x01, 0x02, 0x04 and 0x08 are those above. The remaining values, 0x10 through 0x80, are assigned under the IETF Review policy, which requires a description and a reference to an RFC approved by the IESG.
sections.eli5: A librarian keeps the official list of tick boxes. Four are taken and four are saved for later, to be handed out only after careful review.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: Routers that implement the additional CV types are subject to the same security considerations as RFC 5085, RFC 5880, RFC 5881 and RFC 6428. The document says it raises no additional security issues beyond those.
sections.eli5: Nothing new to worry about here. The same safety rules as before still apply.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Length of the sub-TLV including type and length; minimum 4.

fields.name: CV Type
fields.desc: Bitmask of the CV monitoring types the PE supports.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.desc: Zeroes on transmit, ignored on receive.

items.desc: Independent mode for PW Fault Detection and AC/PW Fault Status Signaling.

items.desc: Independent mode for PW Fault Detection only.
